name: BMW 335i (E92)
engine: 3.0L N54B30 twin-turbocharged inline-six (2007–2010); the 2011+ E92 switched to the single-turbo N55
reliability: 6/10 — the E92 335i put BMW's first modern twin-turbo six into the 3 Series and made it a tuner legend: a simple flash adds 50–70+ hp, because the underrated N54 has huge headroom. That upside comes with the N54's maintenance reputation — a high-pressure fuel pump that was the subject of a major recall/class action, wastegate rattle, fuel injector failures, and a plastic charge pipe that cracks. It's a hugely rewarding, bargain-priced performance coupe for an owner who goes in eyes-open and keeps the fuel system healthy. (The 2011+ N55 cars resolved the HPFP and wastegate woes.)
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate · Maintenance ~$1,000/yr (N54 fuel system and turbos are the big items; the N55 is easier) · Cheap to buy, not always cheap to keep — budget for the known N54 jobs
popular_mods: A tune (JB4 or a flash) — the N54's signature mod, big safe gains from stock turbos
An aluminum charge pipe to replace the crack-prone factory plastic one
An updated HPFP and walnut-blast of the intake valves (direct-injection carbon buildup)
An upgraded intercooler and downpipes to support a tune
Honest take: budget for the fuel system (HPFP, injectors) before chasing power — a healthy N54 is a fast, cheap thrill; a neglected one is a money pit
oil_interval: Every 5,000–7,500 miles (short of BMW's condition-based interval)

generations.E92 335i, N54 (2007–2010): The car that defined the 'N54 era' — twin-turbo torque, effortless real-world pace, and enormous tuning headroom that made it the aftermarket's darling. Also the most maintenance-heavy of the E9x sixes.
generations.E92 335i, N55 (2011–2013): A mid-cycle switch to the single-turbo N55 with Valvetronic — still 300 hp / 300 lb-ft, but it resolved the HPFP and wastegate-rattle problems, making it the easier-living choice.

common_issues: N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure — major recall/class action on 2007–2010 cars
Turbo wastegate rattle from bushing wear (N54)
Plastic charge pipe cracking under boost
Electric water-pump/thermostat failure and oil-filter-housing gasket leaks
maintenance_tips: On an N54 car, confirm the HPFP and injectors have been updated or budget for them
Fit an aluminum charge pipe and keep an eye out for wastegate rattle
Walnut-blast the intake valves periodically — direct injection means carbon buildup
Replace the electric water pump proactively around 80k–100k miles
If you want the fast N54 experience with fewer headaches, seek a 2011+ N55 car

engine.detail: 3.0L N54B30 twin-turbo inline-six — 300 hp and 300 lb-ft from 1,400 rpm via two small parallel turbos (2007-2010; the 2011+ E92 switched to the single-turbo N55). Massively tunable — a simple flash adds 50-70+ hp.
engine.watch: Turbo wastegate rattle from bushing wear is the classic N54 turbo complaint, and the plastic charge pipe cracks under boost. The electric water pump and thermostat fail (replace proactively around 80k-100k), the oil-filter-housing gasket leaks, and direct injection means the intake valves need periodic walnut-blasting for carbon buildup.

fuel.detail: Direct injection with a high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) and piezoelectric injectors — the source of the N54's enormous tuning headroom.
fuel.watch: The HPFP was the subject of a major recall/class action on 2007-2010 cars — confirm it and the piezo injectors have been updated or budget for them. A healthy fuel system is the difference between a cheap thrill and a money pit. (The 2011+ N55 resolved the HPFP and wastegate woes.)

drivetrain.detail: Rear-wheel drive (xDrive AWD optional) through a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed Steptronic torque-converter automatic.
drivetrain.watch: Both gearboxes are durable; service the auto's fluid despite BMW's 'lifetime' claim, and keep the diff/transfer-case fluids fresh on xDrive cars.

suspension.detail: Standard E92 3-series strut front and multilink rear — composed and comfortable rather than track-focused (this isn't the M3).
suspension.watch: Refresh worn bushings and dampers on high-mile cars; coilovers and sway bars are common upgrades.

brakes.detail: Vented front and rear discs with single-piston sliding calipers — sized for a fast coupe, not the M3's compound setup.
brakes.watch: Pads, rotors, and fluid are the only real needs; upgrade the pads and fluid before tracking a tuned car.

body.detail: Steel E92 coupe unibody — a handsome, conventional two-door and the bargain-priced way into the N54.
body.watch: Rock chips and the usual coupe seal and trim wear; well-galvanized, so rust is rare.
